mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the markets and higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) following a 0.25% decrease in FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening labor market, which can lead to lower consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) following a 0.3pp increase in UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which is likely to boost corporate earnings and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of increasing RSAFS.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which can lead to increased corporate profits and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) following a 0.5% increase in INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) combined with an increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a strengthening labor market, which can lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by > 0.2pp and PAYEMS increases by > 100k in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) following a decrease in UNRATE and increase in PAYEMS as described.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) combined with an increase in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals a tightening of supply and increased inflationary pressures, which can lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by > 5% and CPIAUCSL increases by > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) following a decrease in HOUST and increase in CPIAUCSL as described.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to decreased liquidity in the markets and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) following a 0.5% increase in FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) signals a strengthening economy, which can lead to increased corporate profits and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of increasing GDPC1.
